text:
alex: Quick question for HR/benefits team — I'm doing a partial separation (moving to a part-time contractor role) and my 401(k) has a small loan and a recent RMD-like rollover hold. Can I elect to pay off just the loan portion now and leave the rest for a direct rollover after separation? Any vendor timing concerns with the payroll vendor migration next month?

marie: Short answer: you can pay the loan separately to the plan administrator (ACH/wire) and still do a direct rollover of the remaining vested balance later. Two caveats: 1) outstanding loans not repaid at termination may be reported as taxable distributions; 2) you must coordinate timing with payroll cutoffs if you want final-paycheck withholding.

benefitsbot: PlanNote: "PlanAdmin permits partial repayments prior to termination. Loans cannot be rolled into IRAs. Direct trustee-to-trustee rollovers permitted for eligible vested balances. Payroll-based loan repayments must be authorized before the final payroll cutoff to be included in the last pay period."

alex: Specifics — loan ID 881234, balance $1,080. I also have a pending rollover authorization on file but it's marked 'on hold' by the custodian pending paperwork. Migration window: 2026-10-12 -> 2026-10-16. My separation effective date: 2026-10-18. Will migration break the rollover or repayment flows?

payroll: If the rollover paperwork is sitting with the custodian, PlanAdmin can still process a trustee transfer as long as we have receiving acct info and instructions filed before separation. Migration only impacts payroll systems; it does not block PlanAdmin trustee transfers. HOWEVER, if you want payroll withholding on your final paycheck (to pay loan), we need LOAN_PAY_AUTH submitted by 2026-10-09 EOD so it can be configured before the vendor cutover.

liam: If you do an ACH to PlanAdmin today and cc payroll@redwood, we can reconcile quickly and mark the loan as paid so the rollover isn't reduced. PlanAdmin ACH details are on the benefits portal. If you're short on time, do the ACH — it's the safest route around migrations.

alex: Got it. If I pay the $1,080 via ACH now, will PlanAdmin accept and immediately remove the loan hold so the rollover moves forward? Or is there a posting delay?

benefitsbot: PlanAdmin posting note: ACH payments generally post within 1-3 business days. Once posted, PlanAdmin updates the participant record and releases any loan-related holds. We recommend initiating ACH at least 3 business days before your separation to avoid race conditions during cutovers.

marie: Action steps for alex: 1) Initiate ACH/wire to PlanAdmin today and include LoanID 881234 in payment reference. 2) CC payroll@redwood and benefits@planadmin.com so we can reconcile. 3) If ACH timing looks tight, submit a signed LOAN_PAY_AUTH to payroll by 2026-10-09 as backup. 4) After payment posts, request PlanAdmin to proceed with the trustee-to-trustee rollover for the remaining balance.

alex: One more: will the small loan payoff create any tax reporting quirks I should expect on Form 1099-R or W-2?

liam: If you repay before termination, there should be no distribution and no 1099-R for the loan. If unpaid and treated as distribution, PlanAdmin issues 1099-R. Payroll withholding used to pay a loan on final pay is reflected in payroll/benefits reconciliation but not taxed as a distribution if it clears the loan. If any portion is distributed, it will be reported on 1099-R and may be taxable.

marie: Also, because you're moving to a contractor role that will be paid via a different payment channel, ensure you DO NOT accept any rollover checks made payable to you personally. Always request trustee-to-trustee transfer. If you get a check made out to you, forward it to PlanAdmin immediately and do not deposit it — otherwise the 20% withholding may apply.

alex: Thanks! I'll ACH now and cc payroll. Will report back when PlanAdmin confirms posting. :thumbsup:
